$comment: Every model GLASSWALL runs, where its files live, and what we have actually measured. A metric with status 'target' is an acceptance threshold, NOT a result. 'measured' is a real number. 'measured_below_target' is a criterion we FAILED and are recording rather than lowering. Nothing here is fetched at runtime: run `bash ml/fetch-models.sh` once to vendor the assets, after which the extension loads every one of them through chrome.runtime.getURL().

models.name: Tiny 2-layer MLP
models.purpose: Inference spike fixture (P1-B). Not used in the pipeline.

models.name: Xenova/bert-base-NER (ONNX, int8)
models.purpose: P8 local NER. Advisory evidence for fusion; never authoritative for Tier 1.
models.license: MIT (model weights); the underlying bert-base-NER is Apache-2.0
models.trainingData: CoNLL-2003 English (Reuters newswire, 1996). Labels: PER, LOC, ORG, MISC.

install.note: Vendored by `bash ml/fetch-models.sh`. apps/extension/public/ is gitignored, so these files are fetched once per clone rather than committed - 113MB of weights does not belong in git history. Transformers.js is pinned to this directory via env.localModelPath with env.allowRemoteModels=false; there is no CDN fallback and a missing file degrades to ner_unavailable, never to a network call.

alsoRequired.note: onnxruntime-web .wasm binaries, copied by the same script from the ORT build that @huggingface/transformers itself depends on - a mismatched ORT version and JS glue will not load. env.backends.onnx.wasm.wasmPaths points here; without it ORT fetches its runtime from jsdelivr.

metrics.name: span_f1
metrics.note: 25 generator seeds, 50 gold spans, 2026-09-01. Precision 1.00, recall 0.92. Node CPU EP; accuracy is device-independent.

metrics.name: recall_person_name
metrics.note: On the generator's Indian first/last name pool. Contradicts the pre-measurement assumption that CoNLL-2003 training would depress Indian-name recall.

metrics.name: recall_street_address
metrics.note: FAILS the >=0.90 criterion. All 4 misses are bare Bengaluru localities with no road/street token (BTM Layout, Hebbal); the model predicts no location at all for them. Addresses containing Road/Street are found reliably.

metrics.name: model_size_bytes
metrics.note: FAILS the <=30MB criterion by 3.5x. No published quantization of bert-base-NER fits: int8/uint8 108.5MB, q4f16 93.7MB (smallest), bnb4 139.2MB, q4 144.5MB, fp16 215.8MB, fp32 431.2MB. Meeting 30MB requires a smaller encoder, not a smaller number format.

metrics.name: p50_ms_webgpu_2000_tokens
metrics.note: Not measurable in node: transformers.js exposes only the 'cpu' device there. Must be measured in the extension.

metrics.name: ep_parity_webgpu_vs_wasm
metrics.note: Neither EP can be instantiated in node, so parity is unverified.

knownGaps: MEASURED: bare Indian locality names without a road/street token (BTM Layout, Hebbal, Koramangala, Whitefield) are missed entirely - no location is predicted at all. This drives STREET_ADDRESS recall to 0.84 and is the model's clearest weakness on this data.

MEASURED: house numbers are excluded from predicted spans ('42 Residency Road' comes back as 'Residency Road'). Harmless under IoU matching, but a redaction rect drawn from the span will not cover the number.
No STREET_ADDRESS label exists. Addresses are inferred from LOC, which conflates a city, a state and a street.

NOT observed, contrary to expectation: Indian personal names scored 1.00 recall on the generator's pool. The CoNLL-2003 concern is real in principle but did not appear here - do not repeat it in MODEL_CARD.md as though it were measured. The pool is 30 first names x a last-name list in a clean clinical template, so this is not a hard test either.
Latin script only. Devanagari, Tamil and Bengali names are not recognised.
Case-sensitive: all-caps or all-lowercase form fields degrade sharply.
Newswire register. Clinical and transactional prose is out of domain.
mitigations: NER is one source among several; fusion uses noisy-OR, so a missed entity can still be caught by a deterministic recognizer or by OCR.

HONEST RESIDUAL: a bare locality name in free text with no other signal WILL pass. Explain-or-redact masks regions the DOM cannot account for, but a text node is accounted for, so an NER miss inside one is not covered. This is a real leak path, not a mitigated one.

models.name: Tesseract.js 5 (LSTM, English)
models.purpose: P9 targeted OCR on regions the DOM cannot explain. Never full-page.

install.note: Vendored by `bash ml/fetch-models.sh` from node_modules plus the tessdata release. All three of workerPath, corePath and langPath point here; workerBlobURL is false (MV3 CSP blocks blob: workers) and cacheMethod is 'none' so it cannot decide to re-fetch language data. This is the single most likely way a CDN fetch gets into the repo.

metrics.name: box_error_px
metrics.note: Coordinate round trip is pure geometry and is measured without the engine.

knownGaps: WASM only. There is no WebGPU backend, so the WebGPU latency target does not apply to OCR.
Rotated, skewed or low-contrast text degrades sharply; watermarks are effectively unreadable.
English only. Devanagari and other scripts would need their own traineddata, which would roughly double the bundle.
mitigations: A crop that times out or cannot be read is reported unexplained and masked, so a bad read never produces a clean-looking region.
Budget of 6 crops per step at 512px; regions beyond the budget are masked rather than skipped.
